THIS WEEK IN LOCAL GOVERNMENT

The Wausau City Council passed a lead service line replacement ordinance after contentious debate, while Marathon County committees moved forward on redevelopment of the UWSP Wausau campus and a law enforcement contract dispute with Rib Mountain.

  • The Wausau City Council approved a lead service line replacement ordinance (file 260921) after lengthy debate over resident costs, and unanimously rejected a permanent billboard easement at 1514 North Third Street.
  • Marathon County committees directed staff to begin lease negotiations with the Marathon Center for Arts and Culture and to engage all four UWSP Wausau campus redevelopment proposals for potential negotiation.
  • The Wausau Finance Committee voted 4-1 to kill a solar array project at the water treatment facility after the city lost an EPA grant, and unanimously approved a sole-source purchase of Lucas CPR devices for the fire department.
  • The Wausau Infrastructure Committee took no formal action on boulevard snow plowing but directed the city attorney to research Wisconsin statute 346.05(2) after about 15 residents urged a return to center-boulevard plowing.
  • The Village of Weston's Community Life & Public Safety Committee recommended adding alternating-day parking restrictions on six high-density streets from October 31 to May 1 to aid winter snow removal.
  • The Kronenwetter Village Board is set to appoint an interim clerk, establish an interim wage, and vote on a zoning change for 1904 Lea Road at its Monday meeting.

Coming up: Monday brings a full slate, including the Wausau School Board's regular meeting at 5:00 PM — where the 2026-2027 budget and tax levy are on the agenda — and the Kronenwetter Village Board at 6:00 PM. Later in the week, the DC Everest School Board meets Wednesday at 6:30 PM and Marathon County's HR, Finance & Property Committee convenes Thursday at 5:00 PM.
